title: Epoch alignment and speculative kernel scorer to prevent capture drift in staggered multi-stream decodes
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: We observe intermittent correctness and nondeterministic replay failures during staggered prefill+decode workloads on multi-stream CUDA-graph deployments. Root causes appear to be slight epoch misalignment across streams combined with speculative kernel choices that are optimal for occupancy but incompatible with the captured graph layout (quantization layout / fused-attn code-path mismatches). This ticket proposes an approach that (1) aligns stream "epochs" at capture boundaries with a lightweight quiesce handshake, (2) computes a speculative kernel score at scheduling time that penalizes potential capture incompatibilities, and (3) defines a soft-fallback protocol for safe on-the-fly recapture or transient non-graph decode without user-visible errors.
acceptance_criteria: Capture drift rate (measured as percent of captures that later require a fallback/re-capture) reduced by >= 80% on canary workloads compared to baseline
Replay error rate on multi-stream CI harness reduced to < 0.01% for the canonical chat and completion traces
No user-visible increase in P50 latency more than 5% across production workloads after canary rollout (documented in rollout notes)
Observability: new metrics capture_epoch_offset, speculative_kernel_score, and fallback_count emitted; dashboards created and linked
Automated tests added to the replay harness that simulate staggered prefill to validate deterministic replay for at least 5000 randomized seeds
tasks: Design epoch alignment handshake (Asha) — define message format and timeout semantics
Implement speculative kernel scorer in scheduler (Luis) — score combines occupancy, quant mismatch, kernel ABI compatibility, and memory headroom
Add quiesce/handshake to capture path and ensure no deadlocks (eng pair: Luis + Mei)
Wire new metrics and add dashboard (Observability team)
Add fallback paths: 1) transient non-graph decode, 2) capture-with-slight-layout-adjustment, 3) emergency recapture — implement prioritized fallback sequence
Create CI fuzz harness test for staggered prefill sequences and integrate into nightly
comments: 2026-02-21 - Asha Raman: Spike completed. Proof-of-concept handshake introduced two-phase quiesce with 2ms timeout; prevented 60% of observed drift in local tests. Needs perf tuning to avoid increasing tail latency.

2026-02-27 - Luis Ortega: Implemented first pass of the speculative_kernel_score. Score components: occupancy (0..1), quant_mismatch_penalty (0..2), kernel_abi_mismatch (0 or 1), mem_headroom_factor (0..0.5). Normalized to 0..1. High score means prefer non-graph path or recapture.

2026-03-02 - Mei Chen: Verified that quiesce handshake does not deadlock with existing prefill window logic. Found an edge case when streams join mid-prefill; added 'join-window' backoff to handle late arrivals.
2026-03-05 - Observability: Dashboard draft created. Added metrics capture_epoch_offset_ms, speculative_kernel_score_p90, fallback_count/hour. Need tagging per-customer for Dedicated runs.

2026-03-08 - Performance note: On canary fleet with 100 nodes, enabling handshake increased median prefill latency by 2.8% and tail p99 by 6% before kernel scorer; with scorer enabled we reduced p99 delta to 3.1%.

2026-03-10 - Luis Ortega: Began implementing soft-fallback sequence. For highest-scoring cases we first try a local recapture that only rebinds the attention kernel; if that fails or exceeds 12ms, we fallback to transient non-graph decode and schedule background full recapture. Added telemetry to track fallback durations and reasons.
